content: This document outlines important information regarding the use, side effects, precautions, and storage of a medication, as well as guidance on drug interactions and overdose management. Below is a detailed explanation: Side Effects: Common side effects of this medication may include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fatigue, dizziness, changes in vaginal bleeding, breast tenderness, and headaches. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of side effects. If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact your healthcare provider for advice. Precautions: Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other progestins (such as norethindrone), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. The medication may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. While it does pass into breast milk, it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain drugs may reduce the effectiveness of emergency birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples of such drugs include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), St. John’s wort, seizure medications (e.g., barbiturates, carbamazepine, felbamate, phenytoin, primidone, topiramate), and certain HIV drugs (e.g., nelfinavir, nevirapine), among others. Overdose: An overdose of this medication is highly unlikely. However, if someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. For non-emergency situations, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on safe disposal. Important Notes: This document provides a summary of information and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Additional Information: If you are comparing formulary status for this medication with other drugs in the same class, you may need to create a list of plans. This list can be saved and edited as needed. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most up-to-date formulary information, as individual plans may vary, and formulary details are subject to change. This information was last revised in May 2024.
